newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian euthanasia vote uncertain - poll.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian euthanasia vote uncertain - poll.

text.p: The success or failure of a controversial Australian bill on euthanasia remains uncertain with the final result likely to come down to six votes, a poll published on Monday has found.
The Australian newspaper's poll, taken last week, suggests that neither side would have an outright majority if the vote was held in the upper house of parliament, the Senate, today.
The newspaper said the balance was held by senators who had either not made up their minds on the issue, or were unwilling to reveal their views.
But the poll found most senators -- those both supporting or opposing the bill -- believed the bill would be passed with a majority of two to six votes.
The poll said 24 senators would vote for the bill, 20 would vote against, 24 did not give an opinion and did not respond to the survey.

The lower house of parliament, the House of Representatives, last week passed the bill, which seeks to overturn the remote Northern Territory's legislation allowing terminally-ill patients to end their lives.
The bill has been referred to a Senate commitee for consideration with a report expected on February 24.
